hypotheses.justification: In fact, both finite presentation and flatness can be deleted together. Unfold rankAtStalk at p directly. Since 0 belongs to p.asIdeal, every element of p.asIdeal.primeCompl is nonzero, hence a non-zero-divisor in the domain S. Apply IsLocalization.rank_eq and IsLocalizedModule.rank_eq with this complement to identify the localized rank with Module.rank S M. Then hrank and Module.finrank_eq_of_rank_eq finish. These lemmas require neither hypothesis and cover n = 0 and the zero module as well.

Flatness is unnecessary even without finite presentation: rankAtStalk is defined as the finrank of the localized module, not its residue-field fiber dimension. At any prime p, its complement consists of non-zero-divisors because S is a domain. IsLocalization.rank_eq followed by IsLocalizedModule.rank_eq therefore gives localized rank n from hrank; Module.finrank_eq_of_rank_eq gives the conclusion. This also works for torsion modules and n = 0.
